mintAuthority.summary: Canonical sUSDx shares are issued against deposited USDx, with pending-request cancellation restoring previously burned shares. Native USDx issuance is inherited from usdx-axis. The wrapper is upgradeable under a separate two-day timelock, while its governance Safe can change accounting and redemption parameters directly.

controls.evidence: asset() returned canonical USDx at block 26107703, and getVaultState() reported solvent=true with assetBalance equal to requiredAssets. Deposits mint pro-rata shares against USDx; requestRedeem burns shares and reserves assets; cancellation re-mints those previously burned shares. Reward funding transfers USDx before vesting. No unrestricted local share-minter role is documented. This is mint-scoped resolution, not a claim of immutable code or absence of inherited parent issuance.

review.evidence: The complete canonical V2 role-event history and current hasRole calls resolve current service, reward, restriction, admin and timelock memberships at block 26110188. Local shares mint through asset-backed deposit accounting and pending-request cancellation; there is no unrestricted share-minter role in the verified implementation. The same 3-of-5 Safe is timelock proposer/executor/canceller and directly controls vault parameters. The known nonzero Safe fallback handler has not received execution-complete review. Parent USDx retains direct Safe mint and offchain reserve-reconciliation risk. Seven-day cooldown eligibility grants no guaranteed servicing completion. The exact verified handler source identifies standard Safe CompatibilityFallbackHandler; the generic handler noninterference question is not a separate native mint-identity gap when modules and the standard guard are none-detected. Independent signer/key-custody evidence remains unavailable. Servicing guarantees belong to redemption review, and inherited parent issuance and reserve uncertainty remain on the parent and Backing domains rather than making this complete local mint census unresolved.

scopedQuestions.question: Axis discloses that the governance Safe's multisig signer keys are held in cold storage on hardware wallets, with a geographically distributed 3-of-5 set inside and outside Axis Labs. What independent evidence binds the five observed signer addresses to separate operators and specifies their recovery and approval policy? Hardware-wallet custody is public but is not an MPC or HSM attestation.
